answer: A sybil farm loses its edge when every identity must prove it occupies a separate environment. A node is paid only for answering an unpredictable local probe: its host clock drift, its chassis temperature curve, its power-cycle history. Clones behind one rack return the same drift and the same thermal line, so one probe fingerprints the whole set and voids its rewards. The attacker then needs a real machine, a real power feed and a real network path per identity, not one script per identity: a jade cutter's bench, a walnut orchard's pump house and a juniper windbreak do not share a clock.
